verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4 T12, bullet 3: 'a relation checker: the reader picks one of the Chevalley-Serre relations and one or two nodes, and the tool displays the matrix on each side of the relation and whether they are equal (chevalleySerre)'. T12 Acceptance: 'choosing the non-minuscule node 2 of D4 shows a failing relation'. SPEC 9.2: 'its acceptance criteria are automated and pass'. build-plan/COMMON.md 4.3: 'A test must fail when the behaviour it guards is removed'. These passages support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read SPEC 4 T12 whole: the bullets and the Acceptance carry no label, no [D] and no 'may'. The [D] of 4.0 covers the common rules, not the relation checker. Tests read at 006f50d (worktree detached there and clean): T12.spec.ts:132-157 (D4 node 2) asserts data-holds 'false', 'not equal' and '10 of 280 relations fail', but never reads a cell of relation-left or relation-right. :234-251 reads both sides only for ef:1,2 on A2, where every cell is '0', and checks serre-e:1,2 by its live text. :504 checks relationSides for ef:1,1, which holds. M8.spec.ts:396-402 (b4) reads the sides for ef:1,1 (both H1) and ef:1,2 (both empty). T12.test.ts:177 checks left equals right for the listed representations, :917 checks ef:1,1 (holds), :1238 reads data-format only, and :1351 checks shownCheck for ef:7,7 (holds). No test reads the displayed sides of a relation whose sides differ. The patch, read as text, changes only T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:906 (check.left becomes check.right). Phase: the heading 'T12. Representation Builder (phase 5)', and the gate is G5. DECISIONS.md P5-A2 entries (:3179-3209) and 'MERGE: P5 stage 5.2' (:3212) record no choice about this. reports/gate-G5.md names gate commit 006f50d and lists no open item on it. No earlier phase 5 round merge report exists under /home/user/mutation_game/reports/. No '// regression' test covers it. Wrong part: the finding's quote 'acceptance of T12 as automated tests' comes from build-plan/rosters/phase-5.json gateItems[2], not from SPEC 9.1, whose G5 cell reads 'golden tests through phase 5; every relation checks in the tool'. SPEC 9.2 states the same requirement, so the cause stands.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because T12 bullet 3 and its Acceptance have no 'may' or other qualifier; R2 fails because the finding reads the passage correctly (only its 9.1 quote is really the roster's gate item, and 9.2 says the same); R3 fails because T12 is phase 5 at gate G5; R4 does not apply because there is no mathematical disagreement; R5 fails because the passage is not [D] and no fragment or MERGE entry records a choice about it; R6 fails because no record exists in gate-G5.md, no earlier P5 round exists and no regression test exists. Severity none: the rubric names this case at blocker ('a test suite that passes while the behaviour is absent') if the two sides are part of 'shows a failing relation', and at minor ('a test that could be stronger without being wrong') if they belong to bullet 3 alone. It does not name it at major, the level claimed.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4 T12, bullet 1: 'the orbit drawn in layers with edges coloured by node'. SPEC 6.3: 'Edges of orbit graphs are coloured by node from a palette of eight ... Label k takes colour k for k=1,...,8'. RED-TEAM-COMMON 2: a finding may be 'a specific way in which a test ... proves less than it says'. These passages support the finding for the edge colours.
verdicts.evidence: The edge bullet of 6.3 carries [V] only for its contrast ratios. The [D] marks of 6.3 sit on the view accents, the typefaces and the Satake decoration, not on this bullet. Tests read at 006f50d: T12.spec.ts:163-181, titled 'edges coloured and labelled by node', asserts only that the two A2 edges have 2 distinct stroke colours. T12.test.ts:1180-1203 checks data-edge-node, data-edge-from, data-edge-to and data-step in the edge markup, but not its style. contrast.test.ts:154-157 tests edgeColour(k) itself, not the argument OrbitLayers.svelte:78 passes to it. The patch, read as text, changes edgeColour(e.node) to edgeColour(e.from + 1). On the A2 orbit this gives colours 1 and 2 to the edges of nodes 1 and 2, the same picture. T12.spec.ts:213-215 picks matrix-node 2 and reads only matrix-e. :253-260 reads move-matrix and signed-move only on the default (node 1). T12 is phase 5 at gate G5. No record in DECISIONS.md, gate-G5.md or a regression test. Weaker parts: the matrix node picker is the plan's own feature (DECISIONS.md:3200 'matrices (with a node k picker of its own)', 'the move matrix of node k'). SPEC 4 T12 bullet 4 does not say which node's move is shown, and SPEC 9.2 does not contain the finding's phrase 'every stated behaviour is part of done'. The cause, tests that cannot tell a wrong source from the right one, still stands on the edge colours.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because 6.3 and T12 bullet 1 are unqualified; R2 fails because the finding reads 6.3 correctly (only the second half rests on a plan feature and on a paraphrase of 9.2 rather than a SPEC sentence, and one cause stands); R3 fails because T12 is phase 5 at G5; R4 does not apply because there is no mathematical claim; R5 fails because the edge-colour sentence is not [D] and no decision covers its test; R6 fails because there is no record. Minor is the rubric's level for 'a test that could be stronger without being wrong'.

verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 6.6, field table, `start`: 'the starting position; default: all ones for numbers, one Martian in the first city for populations' (unlabelled, not [D]). SPEC 4.0 [D], Board pickers: 'resets start and moves to the tool's defaults for that board'. SPEC 4.0 [D], Configuration: '`default` is the state described in this section'. SPEC 4 T12 names no start ('for a chosen position mu'). These passages leave the finding standing, with an ambiguity for the owner.
verdicts.evidence: SPEC 6.6 opens 'Its fields for the game tools:' and, in the same paragraph, lists T12's own fields 'node and relation (T12)'. SPEC 7.4 says 'A tool's state is the object of section 6.6'. T12's state has coords 'numbers', a start and moves for a string viewer that plays free firing (DECISIONS.md:3197). 4.0 says 'the tool's defaults' and 6.6 says 'the tool's default' on a tool's own route, but neither gives or frees a value other than 6.6's. T12's entry names none, and M8's beat 1 figure (strings through (1,0) and (2,0)) is the string-viewer figure, not the tool default. The build at 006f50d: t12/model.ts:269-281 has omegaStart, commented 'the default start, plan', and defaultsFor sets start to omegaStart(board, node). t12/config.ts:38 sets the default preset start to [1, 0]. T12.test.ts:839 pins defaultsFor('D4', 2).start as [0,1,0,0]. Record: decisions/P5-A2.md, folded at DECISIONS.md:3179 'P5-A2: boards offered, the picker, the default state', records start [1, 0] and omega_i on every pick with 'What the specification left open: the default board, node and start. Default used: the plan's (instruction 5.2)'. The plan file says 'Default state (plan; T12 states none)'. 'MERGE: P5 stage 5.2' (:3212) folds the fragment and lists four accepted deviations, none of them the start. ':3332 MERGE ... repaired after review' does not mention it. The start is not on the known-and-decided list of P5-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS.md. It is not a section 10 default and has no owner's answer. For comparison, other tools follow 6.6's default or record and justify a departure (P4-A4 for T11, DECISIONS.md:2194).
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence permits a default start other than 6.6's (4.0 [D] defers to 'the tool's defaults' without fixing or freeing their value, and T12 names no start); R2 fails because the finding reads 6.6 as written and T12's state is a 6.6 state with coords numbers, although 'Its fields for the game tools' and 'the tool's default' leave the owner room to read 6.6's value as a fallback only, an ambiguity that goes to the owner; R3 fails because T12 is phase 5 at G5; R4 does not apply because the oracle is not involved; R5 fails because decisions/P5-A2.md holds a builder's default that says the specification left the start open, not a [D] text, a section 10 default or an owner's answer, and MERGE did not list it among the accepted deviations; R6 fails because there is no record. Raise to major because, if the claim holds, a stated default of a field is wrong, which the rubric lists as major ('a behaviour the specification states is missing or wrong') and does not list as minor.
